extracted.intended_audience: AP English Literature teachers, readers/graders, and students preparing for the AP prose analysis free-response question
extracted.subtask_description: Scoring rubric for the AP English Literature & Composition prose-analysis free-response question: a 6-point scoring system organized into three rows (Thesis; Evidence and Commentary; Sophistication) that defines what earns 0–4/0–1 points on each dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring structure: 6-point scale across 3 rows
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall scoring framework: student responses are evaluated on three separate rows (A, B, C) that together produce a 6-point score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rows: A = Thesis (0–1), B = Evidence AND Commentary (0–4), C = Sophistication (0–1). Scores are assigned per row according to the descriptors; the sum yields the student's score out of 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Row A — Thesis (0–1 point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion assesses whether the response presents a defensible interpretation of the passage as a thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1 point: 'Responds to the prompt with a thesis that presents a defensible interpretation of the passage.' 0 points: No defensible thesis; merely restates the prompt; or describes the passage instead of making a claim. Anti-patterns: restating the prompt, summary/description without an interpretive claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Row B — Evidence AND Commentary (0–4 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the selection of textual evidence and the quality of commentary tying evidence to the thesis/line of reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 pts: Specific evidence in service of a line of reasoning; commentary consistently explains how evidence supports the line of reasoning. 3 pts: Specific evidence supports all claims; commentary explains how it supports the thesis. 2 pts: Some specific evidence; commentary explains relation to thesis but is uneven. 1 pt: General evidence; minimal or incoherent commentary. 0 pts: Simply restates thesis; offers no evidence or commentary. Emphasis: moves beyond quoting to explaining how chosen details function in support of the interpretation; coherence and sustained connection to thesis/argument raise the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Row C — Sophistication (0–1 point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional point awarded for responses that demonstrate sophistication of thought or control of rhetorical/analytical approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1 point may be earned by accomplishing one of the following: identifying and exploring complexities or tensions within the passage; illuminating the interpretation by situating it in a broader context; accounting for and responding to alternative interpretations; or employing a style that is consistently vivid and persuasive. This point requires more than surface-level analysis—shows nuance, complexity, and persuasive/controlled prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied quality criteria for prose-analysis responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualities of passages and analyses that are rewarded by the rubric—what counts as a 'complex' passage and what analytic moves demonstrate insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses that surface complexities are rewarded, including: shifting, contradictory, or paradoxical elements; multi-layered meanings (surface meaning plus subtext); identification of stylistic choices that produce specific effects (diction, syntax, imagery, tone, point of view, structure); and evidence that the writer made intentional craft decisions. Guidance implies evaluative preference for demonstrations that evidence is used to show purposeful craft and layered meaning rather than mere summary.
